properties.name: RECURRENCE (2026-10-05, measured on 0.79.0): a store ahead of its export is said only in loop_status's `next`, only when the store holds a record of that export, and only as a node count. A copy written another way (`--export > file`, another machine, an old commit) leaves no record, so loop_status says nothing. The field check `--call loop_status | head -40` showed only the artifact block. The fix is being built on feat/loop-status-says-what-is-unexported
properties.statement:
Field log entry [friction] of 2026-10-05 (art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, lines 338-344), from upgrading 20 stores to 0.79.0: "the upgrade recipe says `--call loop_status | head -40` — anything unexported?, but loop_status's first 40 lines are the artifact block (`unmeasurable` remote URIs on a member store), and `sync_status` says by design 'BEING AHEAD OF THE RECORD IS NOT REPORTED'. No served tool answers 'does this store hold work its export lacks?'" Workaround: export to /tmp and compare with the committed copy. Idea: a sync_status flag, or a loop_status headline "ahead of <export>: N nodes / M edges".

THE RECIPE WAS NOT REFLOW2'S. The `head -40` step came from a recipe the maintainer's agent wrote in chat (fact:the-0-79-0-install-near-miss-came-from-a-recipe-written-in-chat-not-from-reflow2-2026-10-05). UPDATING.md has no such step. What the step exposed is reflow2's.

RE-MEASURED on 0.79.0, through --call on scratch stores:
- First store: its export was written by a writing call (`--export-to docs/design/d.json`), and then a second requirement was written with --no-export. loop_status: clean: true, and a `next` line, "This graph holds 2 node(s), and the most complete record it is in step with ... holds 1, so 1 node(s) here are in no record". sync[0]: state in_step, live_nodes 2, export_nodes 1. `since_export: true`: unexported_nodes 1, unexported_sample [req:two]. compare_designs with base_path lists the added node.
- Second store, the same, except the export was written by `reflow2-mcp --export > docs/design/x.json`. The store keeps no record of that copy. loop_status: clean: true, next: [], no sync block. since_export says no committed record was readable, and counts both nodes as new.
- loop_status prints its keys alphabetically, so `artifacts` comes before `next`. On a member whose registered files are remote and unmeasurable, that block fills the first 40 lines.

CLASSIFICATION: still present on 0.79.0, a recurrence of recorded causes. The cheap line is computed from the store's own record of an export it wrote or imported by path (fact:root-cause-a-hosted-session-hears-nothing-about-exports-because-the-only-export-line-rides-a-tracked-export-2026-09-28). And `in_step` describes the record, not the store (fact:defect-nothing-in-the-loop-reports-unexported-work-and-in-step-is-read-as-if-it-did).

The reporter's "no served tool answers" is OVERTURNED IN PART. compare_designs with base_path answers it in full (fact:worked-compare-designs-against-the-committed-export-shows-what-a-live-store-has-not-exported-2026-10-05), and the `next` line answers it as a count when a record exists. Neither is where an upgrade check reads.

BEING FIXED, NOT DUPLICATED HERE: the branch feat/loop-status-says-what-is-unexported (another agent, 2026-10-05, not merged when this was written). It adds `ahead_of_export`: a first line in loop_status, ahead of the artifact block, counting nodes by default, and under since_export the nodes and edges added, changed and removed, with who wrote them. sync_status gets the same field, and a design never exported gets a line of its own. The reporter's idea is that change. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether it sees a committed copy the store holds no record of (the stdout-export case above), other than through the project's configured export.
